flags.detail: The design's own printed false-positive rate (5-6%) for the 'confirmation' was computed against a projected precision (sigma=0.0015) that never materialized; the actual achieved precision (sigma=0.0087) yields ~32% FP, an order-of-magnitude weaker evidential claim than what was pre-registered as the headline number, and the ORIGINAL prereg's 5-6% figure is what the campaign's closing 'OUTCOME A' language rode on before the honesty-discount paragraph appeared.

The adjudicated claim itself is a textbook case of numerology-by-type-coincidence (matching small SM beta-function integers to framework integers by size alone); this arc correctly diagnoses and kills it, which is itself worth noting as a positive discipline example rather than a flaw of this arc.

The refuted claim itself (an external/incoming seat's identification of the h0 invariant line with 'the Spin(10) gauge singlet = a dark matter candidate') is a textbook type-coincidence (same dimension, same 27-representation) that this arc correctly kills by exact computation (v0's coefficient at the singlet weight is exactly zero); worth flagging as the pattern this seat exists to catch, and it succeeds.

The correspondence table treats 'phi appearing in the S-transform of R=-I irreps' in both the framework and the Gamma5' literature as 'SAME LOCUS' evidence for the correspondence, when both are independently well-known appearances of phi in A5/SL(2,5) representation theory (a common source, not evidence of a novel match) -- a dimension/value coincidence used to license the correspondence claim.

Cell I's headline identification (the ear's hearing representation IS the Gamma5'-doublet 2-hat') rests on exact character-table equality on the same abstract group SL(2,F5) that both sides happen to reduce to -- a strong invariant, but the deeper physical claim (that this identifies a real flavor-symmetry functor) is explicitly NOT yet established (the modular-form assignment leg, L108); the arc itself correctly downgrades the upgrade to 'candidate functor' rather than 'functor', so this is a self-flagged rather than silent instance, but it is still fundamentally a match-of-representation-labels on a common finite group, not a derivation of a physical mechanism connecting the two domains.

chat1's original handoff (archived verbatim in this arc) frames the golden-word/golden-stage relationship as a self-selecting fixed point ('the object selects the stage that selects it... this is not circular... a fixed point that proves itself by being consistent'). FINDINGS.md explicitly disciplines this as 'FIREWALLED (a reading, not a theorem)' and does not adopt it, but the rhetorical structure is preserved verbatim in the committed handoff file and could be mistaken for an established result by a later reader who skips FINDINGS' correction.
